claims.text: Equiatomic CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi (Cantor alloy) can have single-phase FCC structures.
CrCoNi has a low stacking-fault energy and a high propensity for deformation twinning.
The relevant initial state is homogenized and coarse-grained.
High-strain-rate loading induces a higher density of nanoscale deformation twins than quasi-static loading.
The structural mediator is a dynamically generated network of nanoscale twins and coherent twin boundaries.
A slight Mn addition to CrCoNi increases its stacking-fault energy.
Increasing stacking-fault energy suppresses deformation twinning in the proposed chemically modified control.
Twin boundaries impede dislocation motion.
Deformation twins and their boundaries promote dislocation multiplication or nucleation.
Twin boundaries promote distributed plasticity and thereby delay localization and necking.
Deformation twinning increases the work-hardening rate.
Twinning-controlled deformation contributes to the simultaneous strength and ductility of CrCoNi.
Dynamic loading will produce a higher yield or flow stress than quasi-static or twin-suppressed loading.
Dynamic loading will produce greater uniform elongation than quasi-static or twin-suppressed loading.
Dynamic loading will concurrently increase twin density, strain hardening, strength, and ductility relative to the controls.
Deformation nanotwinning is active in CrCoNi between cryogenic and ambient temperatures and becomes more prominent at cryogenic temperatures.
Sufficiently high strain rates favor rapid dislocation accumulation and dynamic twin nucleation.
Networks of nanotwins have been observed in CrCoNi after extensive deformation.
The quantitative strengthening contribution of deformation twinning and the nature of twinning-induced plasticity remain uncertain.
The magnitude of twin-induced hardening and ductility varies with composition, initial microstructure, and testing conditions.

contradictions.description: CrCoNi is presented as an example of a high-entropy alloy in the initial-state field, while the boundary field acknowledges that the scope includes medium-entropy alloys; the cited evidence specifically classifies CrCoNi as a medium-entropy alloy.

The intervention defines two distinct controls: the same alloy loaded quasi-statically and a chemically modified higher-SFE alloy. The baseline then describes the quasi-static or chemically tuned control collectively as having minimal twinning due to higher SFE, although changing strain rate does not itself change alloy chemistry or intrinsic SFE.
